clue.text: He ultimately guards door

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word guards that follows it

parts.note: a door is an entry, a way in

explanation.surface: A man whose job, in the end, is to protect a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'guards', S, and the door gives ENTRY; the whole clue also describes the man posted at a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch at a gate or doorway.

clue.text: Ears need tuning for this music

indicators.note: tuning adjusts an instrument, so the letters of ears and need are adjusted into a new order

explanation.surface: Listening closely helps a musician tune for a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuning' rearranges EARS plus NEED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece of music sung or played to a lover, often at night.

clue.text: Take a print from this? No

definitions.meaning: in film photography prints are made from the developed film image with reversed tones
a refusal or denial, as in answering in the ...

explanation.surface: A photographer asks whether a print can be made, and gets a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographic prints are made from a film negative, and a negative reply is a no.

clue.text: What American does, seeking office? Get away!

definitions.meaning: in the US a candidate runs for office rather than standing for it

explanation.surface: A US politician's campaign is followed by a cry to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans speak of running for office, and the same phrase is a shout telling someone to flee.

clue.text: Hurrying to southern battle site

parts.note: hurrying is hasting, an old word for hastening

explanation.surface: Rushing towards a battlefield in the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings, on the south coast of England, gives its name to the battle of 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of 1066 is named after this English town in East Sussex, near where it was fought.

clue.text: A top-level meeting on ship

parts.note: a meeting of directors, at the top of a company, is a board meeting, so board

explanation.surface: Company directors convene a meeting on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a vessel or other vehicle is being aboard it.

clue.text: Farewell note found on Japanese floor

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal British goodbye
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A goodbye message left on the floor of a Japanese home.
explanation.walkthrough: TA-TA is a casual British way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatami are woven straw mats used as flooring in traditional Japanese rooms.

clue.text: New weapon is limited

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A newly introduced weapon has restricted capability.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow can mean restricted in scope, as in a narrow outlook or margin.

clue.text: Live among kind of ice

indicators.note: among puts one word in the middle of another

parts.note: a kind is a sort, a type
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Living amid some type of frozen landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' looks like frozen water, but it is the dessert; 'among' is the container signal and 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice, a frozen dessert of fruit juice and sugar.

clue.text: Soldiers' man, temporary head of state

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A soldiers' man rises to rule the country for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules a kingdom in place of a monarch who is a minor, absent or incapable.

clue.text: He extracts some painful admissions

parts.note: reads like a dentist pulling teeth, but describes someone forcing confessions out of a victim by inflicting pain

explanation.surface: A dentist pulls out teeth, which patients admit is painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inflicts pain to force confessions is a torturer.

clue.text: Idea refusal will get one into trouble

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the letters of into are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: The idea that saying no will land you in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the clue's own word 'into' to follow the refusal; 'will get one' only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or concept, an idea.

clue.text: Flower border described by unpoetic language

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the prose goes round the rim

parts.note: prose is ordinary language, not verse
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A garden border full of flowers, written up in plain words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' works like drawing round a shape: the plain language goes round the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower of woods and hedgerows.

clue.text: Make-up of fried dish

definitions.meaning: a thick cosmetic foundation applied with a damp sponge
a thin batter cake cooked in a frying pan

explanation.surface: Asking what goes into a fried dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan-Cake is a brand of stage foundation, and the batter cake is cooked in a pan.

clue.text: Awful German spa

definitions.meaning: ... is the German word for bath, prefixed to spa town names such as Baden-Baden or ... Ems

explanation.surface: A dreadful German spa resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awful is very poor, and German spa towns carry the title Bad, meaning bath.

clue.text: Plunged back, securing nothing — destitute

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside
back says the word for plunged is read from the end to the start

parts.note: plunged into water means dived
O is the zero for nothing

explanation.surface: A diver plunges backwards, catching nothing and ending up penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DIVED into DEVID, and 'securing' holds O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoid and destitute both mean entirely lacking something; destitute of hope is devoid of hope.

clue.text: Make time, a tiny amount

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a meal

explanation.surface: Finding a moment for a tiny bit of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a minute speck, so a tiny amount.

clue.text: Request from bishop, say

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
say signals an example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A bishop making a request, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to ask earnestly, to request.

clue.text: Filled with pity for the mentally unstable

explanation.surface: Feeling compassion for people with mental illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being moved by sympathy is being touched, and a slightly crazy person is called touched.

clue.text: Deportment training is habit, over time

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first part sits above the second

parts.note: a habit is a garment, a dress
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Learning good posture is a routine that takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts DRESS above AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the training of a horse to perform precise, graceful movements, a kind of deportment.

clue.text: Fall of lots of trees holding everyone up

indicators.note: holding means containing the other piece inside

parts.note: a copse is a small wood, many trees together

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: A tree falls in a wood and everyone is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' can suggest autumn, but here it is a falling-down; 'up' turns the word for everyone upside down in this down clue before 'holding' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden fall or giving way.

clue.text: Got one's car back

parts.note: reads like recovering a stolen vehicle, but means drove a car backwards

explanation.surface: A theft victim recovers a stolen vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving a car in the backward direction is to have put it into reverse gear.

clue.text: Love to go into wood as routine

indicators.note: to go into means being put inside the other piece

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Making a habit of walking into the woods for love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, the tennis score of nil; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a groove means being in a settled routine.

clue.text: Messenger's more plain in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: more plain or unadorned is barer

explanation.surface: A messenger is plainer when he speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' sounds out BARER, more plain, as BEARER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearer carries something, such as a message or news, to someone.

clue.text: For which someone may win gold plate

definitions.text: For which someone may win gold plate

parts.words: For which someone may win gold plate
parts.note: reads like a prize of gilded tableware, but describes the heavy plate thrown in athletics for an Olympic gold

explanation.surface: Someone is awarded a gold-plated trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrown athletics event uses a heavy plate-shaped disc, and Olympic winners take gold medals.

clue.text: Doctor, one finally decided, was a boring speaker

indicators.note: finally signals taking the last letter of the word decided

explanation.surface: A doctor finally reached a decision after a long tedious lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To drone is to talk in a dull monotone, the mark of a boring speaker.

clue.text: Heavenly TV?

definitions.meaning: a British satellite television broadcaster shares the name

explanation.surface: Asking whether some television is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite television company; the question mark flags the brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavens overhead and the satellite broadcaster share this name, used attributively as in a heavenly vault.

clue.text: Dictator's mark of guilt, arresting left

indicators.note: arresting means seizing and holding, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a mark of guilt

explanation.surface: A dictator's guilty record, having locked up left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' puts L inside STAIN; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Free oneself from the land

parts.note: reads like escaping farm work, but means leaving one's home country

explanation.surface: A farmworker escapes the toil of the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving one's own country to settle abroad is to emigrate.

clue.text: Operatic heroine has aged, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are heard spoken

parts.note: has aged means is old

explanation.surface: An opera heroine has got old, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' sounds out IS OLD as the heroine of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess in Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: A little money in bank not long ago

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a small coin, a little money

explanation.surface: A small sum was deposited at the bank a short time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a place for money, but here it is the verb, as in bank on someone; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, a short time back.

clue.text: Students here about to drink beside river

indicators.note: beside places one piece next to the other

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: about here means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Students are about to go drinking by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SUP into PUS, put 'beside' CAM, the river at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university or college, where students study.

clue.text: New tenant perhaps inserted in error

indicators.note: in error means mistakenly placed, so the letters of inserted are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A new tenant was put in a flat by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges INSERTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident lives in a place, as a tenant does.

clue.text: Act as leader and arrange guillotine motion?

definitions.meaning: to set the guillotine blade in motion on someone's neck

explanation.surface: A leader in parliament arranges a guillotine motion to cut debate.
explanation.walkthrough: A guillotine motion in Parliament cuts short debate; here the blade cuts off a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being head means leading, and cutting off a head is what a guillotine does.
